attribution.note: Marcus's own retrospective statement on his own Substack about his own March 2024 predictions. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: A retrospective observation that all seven predictions had held by the post date. The '7 of 7' threshold is kept. The list of seven is not in the excerpt and was identified from the March 10 tweet.

contract.note: Reading 'held strong' as borne out by the evidence is the ordinary reading, and so is auditing each item separately. The vague terms (major advance, modest adoption, modest profits) and the unclear model-counting rule mean interpretation drives the result. The contract flags this openly.

evidence.note: Dated Oct 2024 OpenAI disclosure saying hallucinations remain an open problem. Supports only the hallucination item, and it is a company source.
Google cut Gemini 1.5 Pro prices, effective Oct 2024. Supports the price-competition item only.
OpenAI launched cheaper GPT-4o mini in July 2024. Partly supports the price-competition item, though it is a new small model rather than a matched price cut.
Menlo report (Nov 2024): enterprises use several models and OpenAI's share fell. Supports the weak-moat item. It does not settle durable adoption and shows substantial production use.
St. Louis Fed: modest share of work hours assisted by AI. This measures worker use, not durable corporate deployment, so it cannot decide the adoption item.

reviews.rationale: The evidence supports three items: lasting hallucinations, price competition and weak moats. Nothing in the packet settles the GPT-4-class model count, the absence of a major advance, limited durable adoption, or modest profits. The contract needs all seven borne out to support the claim. Contradiction needs one clearly falsified, and nothing does that either. Result: unresolved.
